div.l: Synging he was and florting al the day
He was as fressh as is the month of May
Short was his goune his sleues long ⁊and wide
Wel coude he sitte an hors and faire ride
And coude songes make and wel endite
Iouste and daunce wel portraye and write
So hoot he loued that be niȝter tale
He slepte nomore than doth a Niting hale
Curteis he was louli and seruisable
And kerue beforn his fader at the table
A yoman he had and seruauntes nomo
As at that tyme for him list ride so
And clad he was in cote and hood of grene
A shef of Pecok arwes briȝt and shene
Vnder his belte he s bar full thriftily
Wel coude he dresse his takill yomanly
His arwes drouped nat with fetheres lowe
And in his hand he bar a miȝti bowe
A notted hed had he with a broun visage
Of woodcraft coude he all the vsage
Vpon̄ his arme he bar a gay bracer
And on that othir side a gay dagger
And be his side a swerd and a bokeler
Harneised well ⁊and sharpe as point of spere
A cristofre on his breest of siluer shene
An horn he bar the baudrik was of grene
A fostere was he sotheli as I gesse
Ther was also a Nonne a Prioresse
That of her smiling was ful simple ⁊and coy
Her grettest othe was be Seint Loy
And she was callid madame Eglentyne
Full well she sang the seruice diuine
Entuned in her nose full semely
And frenssh she spak full wel ⁊and fetisly
Aftir the scole of Stratford of the bowe
For frenssh of Parys was to hir vnknowe
At mete well tauȝt she was with all
She lete no morsell from hir lippes fall
And wett her fyngers in her sauce depe
Wel couthe she carie a morsell and kepe
That no droppe fell on her brest
In curtesie was sette full mochel her lest
Hir ouir lippe wiped she so clene
That in her cuppe no ferthing was ther sene
Of grece whan she had dronke hir drauȝt
Full semeli aftir hir mete she rauȝt
And sikirlich she was of gret disport
And full plesaunt and full amiable of port
And peined hir to counterfete chere
Of court and to ben estatli of manere
And to be holde digne of reuerence
But for to speke of hir conscience
She was so charitable and so pitous
She wolde wepe yef she saw a mous
Caught in a trappe if it were ded or bledde
Of smale houndes had she that she fedde
Of rosted flessh or milk or wastell bred
But sore she wepte yef oon of hem were ded
And if men smot hem with a rodde smerte
All this was conscience of a tender herte
Full semeli hir wimpill pinched was
Hir nose thrilles hir yhen greye as glas
Hir mouth full small and therto softe ⁊and red
But sekirli she had a faire forhed
It was almost a span brod I trowe
For hardli she was nat vndergrowe
Full fetise was hir cloke as I was war
Of small corall aboute hir arme she bar
A peire of bedes the gaudees al of grene
And theron henge a broche of gold ful shene
On wich ther was writen first a crouned A
And aftirward Amor vincit omnia .
An othir Nonne with hir had she
That was hir Chapelein and prestes three
A Monke ther was a faire for the mastrie
An outerider that loued wel venery
A man̄ to ben an Abbott able
Full many a deinte hors had he in stable
And whan he rod men miȝt his bridell hiere
Gyngling in a whistling wynde as clere
And eke as loude as a chapell belle
Ther as this lord was keper of his selle
The rule of seint Maure or of seint Benet
Be cause it was holden somdell streite
This ilke Monke lete olde thinges passe
And holde after the newe world the space
He yaf nat of the text a pulled henne
That seith hunters beth nouȝt holi men̄
Ne that a monk whan that he is recckeles
Is lik a fissh that is waterles
This is to sey a monk withouten̄ his cloistre
But that text halt he nat worth an oistre
And I said his opinion was good
What shuld he studnd make him selue wood
